title: Operative outcomes of appendectomy compared between levels of medical training – a retrospective analysis
summary:
Background:
Removing an inflamed appendix is one of the most common emergency operations. It is performed both by doctors still in training and by highly experienced surgeons. It is not yet clear whether the level of experience of the surgeon influences the outcome of the operation.

Research Question:
This study examines whether surgical outcomes differ depending on the training level of the operating doctor. It compares factors such as complications, duration of the operation, and length of hospital stay.

Methods:
The study is a retrospective analysis of existing medical records from adult patients who underwent surgery between 2020 and 2025 at the hospital. All data are analyzed in anonymized form. No new examinations are carried out, and no patients are contacted.

interventions.name: This study is a single-center retrospective observational analysis including all documented laparoscopic appendectomies performed between January 1, 2020 and June 30, 2025 at the Klinikum Ludwigsburg. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Laparoscopic removal of the appendix performed for confirmed acute appendicitis
Complete clinical documentation available for the case within the study period
Routine clinical data accessible and suitable for retrospective analysis
Exclusion criteria:
Age under 18 years
Primary open surgery
Combined or extended surgical procedures in which the appendix was removed for reasons other than acute inflammation
(e.g., right hemicolectomy for cancer, incidental appendectomy without acute appendicitis)
Incomplete or non-analyzable medical records
